about: Worked reaction schemes as atom-mapped reactant and product SMILES: map numbers tag the atoms whose bonds change; a mapped atom absent from the products leaves; hydrogens are completed from the SMILES. CAPS turns each scheme into a React template (form, break, hydrogen moves, deleted and byproduct atoms) and checks it.

reactions.name: Esterification (acid + alcohol)
reactions.description: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol condense to an ester plus water. The backbone reaction of polyesters (PET, PBS, PLA).

tags.role: the acid's OH oxygen — leaves as part of the water
the alcohol oxygen — survives as the ester bridge O

reactions.note: Read CC(=O)[OH:1] as CH3-C(=O)-OH: C, then a C with a double-bonded O in the (branch), then the OH.

reactions.name: Transesterification
reactions.description: An ester swaps its alkoxy group for a new alcohol. How PET is made industrially from dimethyl terephthalate.

tags.role: the old ester oxygen — leaves with the methyl as methanol
the incoming alcohol oxygen — becomes the new bridge

reactions.name: Anhydride formation (2 acids)
reactions.description: Two carboxylic acids condense to an anhydride plus water. The two acids are identical, so tags are what tell them apart.

tags.role: acid A's OH oxygen — the leaving group
acid B's OH oxygen — survives as the anhydride bridge

reactions.name: Ether condensation (2 alcohols)
reactions.description: Two alcohols condense to an ether plus water (acid-catalysed).

tags.role: leaves in the water
becomes the ether oxygen

reactions.name: PET link (terephthalate + glycol)
reactions.description: A polyester chain-growth step on a real monomer pair: methyl terephthalate + ethylene glycol.

tags.role: the methyl-ester oxygen displaced as methanol
the glycol oxygen that forms the new ester

reactions.note: c1ccc(cc1) is a benzene ring written in aromatic (lower-case) SMILES.

reactions.name: Ring-opening of caprolactone
reactions.description: An alcohol opens the 7-membered lactone ring — the initiation step of polycaprolactone (PCL) growth.

tags.role: the lactone carbonyl carbon (acyl attack site)
the ring oxygen — the C1-O2 ring bond breaks; O2 becomes the chain-end OH
the initiating alcohol oxygen — new ester bridge

reactions.note: No leaving group: a ring-opening just relocates bonds.

reactions.name: Acetal formation (aldehyde + 2 alcohols)
reactions.description: An aldehyde condenses with two alcohols to an acetal plus water — the chemistry that turns PVA into polyvinyl butyral (PVB) safety-glass interlayer.

tags.role: the aldehyde carbon — ends up bonded to BOTH alcohol oxygens
the carbonyl oxygen — leaves as water
the two alcohol oxygens — the acetal's two O bridges

reactions.name: Hemiacetal (aldehyde + alcohol)
reactions.description: The first step of acetal formation: an alcohol adds to the aldehyde C=O; the alcohol's H goes to the carbonyl oxygen.

tags.role: the aldehyde carbon
the carbonyl O — becomes OH
the alcohol oxygen — new C–O bond

reactions.name: Acetal from a hemiacetal + alcohol
reactions.description: The second step of acetal formation: the hemiacetal's OH leaves as water and a second alcohol takes its place.

tags.role: the acetal carbon
the hemiacetal OH — leaves as water
the second alcohol oxygen

reactions.name: Amidation (acid + amine)
reactions.description: A carboxylic acid and an amine condense to an amide plus water — the nylon reaction.

tags.role: acid OH oxygen — leaves in the water
amine nitrogen — forms the new C-N amide bond

reactions.name: Polyamide 6,6 link
reactions.description: Adipic acid + hexamethylenediamine forming one amide link, with both far chain ends left free to keep reacting.

tags.role: the reacting acid OH — leaves as water
the reacting amine N — only ONE end of each monomer is tagged; the other ends stay free

reactions.name: Acid chloride + amine
reactions.description: The fast interfacial-polymerisation route to polyamides (the nylon rope trick). HCl instead of water leaves.

tags.role: the chlorine — a leaving atom: present in the reactants, absent from the products (it departs as HCl, which is not drawn because hydrogen halides cannot be force-field typed)
the amine nitrogen — new amide bond

reactions.name: Acid chloride + alcohol
reactions.description: Ester formation via the activated acid — fast and irreversible.

tags.role: the chlorine — a leaving atom, expelled as HCl (not drawn)
the new ester oxygen

reactions.name: Anhydride + amine (amic acid)
reactions.description: An amine opens a cyclic anhydride to an amic acid — step 1 of every polyimide synthesis.

tags.role: the attacked carbonyl carbon
the ring oxygen — the C1-O2 bond breaks; O2 becomes a free COOH oxygen
the amine nitrogen — new amide bond to C1

reactions.name: Amic acid → imide (cyclisation)
reactions.description: The amic acid closes to a five-membered imide ring, expelling water — step 2 of polyimide synthesis.

tags.role: the amide nitrogen — forms the second N-C bond, closing the ring
the free-acid carbonyl carbon it attacks
the acid OH — leaves as water

reactions.name: Epoxide + amine
reactions.description: The workhorse epoxy-cure reaction: an amine opens the ring at the less hindered carbon; the epoxide oxygen becomes a secondary OH.

tags.role: the substituted ring carbon (keeps the O as OH)
the epoxide oxygen — the O2-C3 bond breaks; O2 stays on C1
the terminal CH2 — the attacked carbon
the amine nitrogen — new C-N bond to C3

reactions.name: Epoxide + carboxylic acid
reactions.description: A carboxylic acid opens an epoxide to a hydroxy-ester. On a trisubstituted (ENR-type) epoxide the acid attacks the TERTIARY carbon.

tags.role: the tertiary epoxide carbon (no H, three C neighbours) — receives the acid oxygen
the epoxide oxygen — C1-O2 breaks; O2 stays on C3 as OH
the secondary epoxide carbon
the attacking acid oxygen — new C1-O4 ester bond

reactions.name: Epoxide + thiol
reactions.description: Thiol-epoxy 'click' cure: fast, efficient, base-catalysed.

tags.role: epoxide O → secondary OH
attacked CH2
the sulfur — new C-S bond

reactions.name: Epoxide + phenol
reactions.description: Phenol opens the epoxide to an aryl ether — the advancement reaction of epoxy resins.

tags.role: epoxide O → OH
attacked CH2
the phenol oxygen — new ether bond

reactions.name: Epoxide + alcohol
reactions.description: Etherification — the side reaction in amine-cured epoxies that creates extra crosslinks at high temperature.

tags.role: epoxide O → OH
alcohol O → ether bridge

reactions.name: Epoxide + water (hydrolysis)
reactions.description: Water opens the epoxide to a 1,2-diol.

tags.role: epoxide O → one OH
water O → the other OH

reactions.name: Epoxide + anhydride
reactions.description: Anhydride cure of epoxies: the ring opens and BOTH oxygens end up as esters — a diester crosslink.

tags.role: epoxide O — acylated by carbonyl C5 (new O2-C5 bond)
ring carbon attacked by the anhydride oxygen O4
anhydride bridge O — its bond to C5 breaks; new bond to C3
one anhydride carbonyl carbon

reactions.name: ENR + maleic acid + ENR (bridge)
reactions.description: Both COOH groups of maleic acid open one epoxide each, bridging two ENR chains — a crosslink. Model compounds stand in for the chains.

tags.role: the two tertiary epoxide carbons — each receives an acid oxygen
the two epoxide oxygens — freed from the tertiary carbons, they stay on :3/:8 as OH groups
the two acid oxygens — the new ester bridges

reactions.note: /C=C\ marks the cis double bond of maleic acid. No atom leaves.

reactions.name: ENR + maleic acid + PBS-COOH (graft)
reactions.description: One maleic-acid COOH opens the ENR epoxide; the other condenses with the PBS terminal COOH to an anhydride, expelling water. The PBS oxygen is retained as the bridge.

tags.role: tertiary ENR carbon — bonded to acid oxygen :4
epoxide O → OH on the secondary carbon
maleic oxygen forming the ester to ENR
maleic acid's second OH — the leaving group (absent from the products)
the PBS carboxyl oxygen — RETAINED as the anhydride bridge

reactions.note: Monomethyl succinate COC(=O)CCC(=O)OH models the true PBS chain end: COOH, two CH2 groups, then the in-chain ester.

reactions.name: ENR + PBS-COOH (direct ester)
reactions.description: The PBS terminal carboxylic acid opens the ENR epoxide directly — no maleic acid involved. Same regiochemistry: attack at the tertiary carbon.

tags.role: tertiary epoxide carbon
epoxide O → OH on the secondary carbon
PBS acid oxygen → the ester link

reactions.name: ENR epoxide + water (diol)
reactions.description: Ring hydrolysis during processing: the epoxide becomes a diol.

tags.role: epoxide O → OH on the secondary carbon
water O → OH on the tertiary carbon

reactions.name: ENR + acid at the SECONDARY carbon
reactions.description: The alternative regiochemistry, for comparison with the tertiary attack: here the acid bonds to the secondary carbon and the OH lands on the tertiary one. Note how ONLY the product drawing changed.

tags.role: epoxide O — stays on the TERTIARY carbon this time
secondary carbon — receives the acid oxygen
acid oxygen → ester on C3

reactions.name: Isocyanate + alcohol (urethane)
reactions.description: The polyurethane bond: an alcohol adds across the N=C of the isocyanate. Pure addition — nothing leaves.

tags.role: the isocyanate nitrogen — its double bond to C3 becomes single and it picks up the alcohol's H
the alcohol oxygen — new bond to C3
the isocyanate carbon — the electrophilic centre

reactions.name: Isocyanate + amine (urea)
reactions.description: The polyurea bond — the fast reaction in PU foams and elastomers.

tags.role: isocyanate N
amine N — new bond to C3
isocyanate C

reactions.name: Isocyanate + water (blowing reaction)
reactions.description: Water converts an isocyanate to an amine and CO2 — the gas that blows PU foams. The isocyanate carbon LEAVES as the CO2 carbon.

tags.role: the nitrogen — ends as a free amine
the water oxygen — ends in the CO2
the isocyanate carbon — follow it into the CO2

reactions.name: Thiol-ene addition
reactions.description: A thiol adds across a C=C double bond (anti-Markovnikov) — the classic UV-cure click reaction.

tags.role: the sulfur — new S-C bond to the terminal carbon
the terminal CH2 of the double bond
the inner alkene carbon — the C2=C3 double bond becomes single; C3 gains an H

reactions.name: Thiol-Michael (thiol + acrylate)
reactions.description: A thiol adds to the activated double bond of an acrylate.

tags.role: sulfur
the acrylate double bond, saturated in the product

reactions.name: Aza-Michael (amine + acrylate)
reactions.description: An amine adds to an acrylate double bond — used in ABC curing and polyaspartics.

tags.role: the nitrogen — new N-C bond
the double bond that saturates

reactions.name: Oxa-Michael (alcohol + acrylate)
reactions.description: An alcohol adds to an acrylate double bond.

tags.role: the oxygen — new O-C bond
the saturating double bond

reactions.name: Diels-Alder (diene + maleic anhydride)
reactions.description: Butadiene and maleic anhydride form a cyclohexene ring in one step — two C-C bonds at once. Used for reversible/self-healing networks.

tags.role: the diene's terminal carbons — each forms one new C-C bond
the diene's inner carbons — the surviving double bond
the anhydride's alkene carbons — the other ends of the two new bonds

reactions.note: The digit pairs 1...1 and 2...2 in the product close its two rings.

reactions.name: Hydrosilylation (Si-H + vinyl)
reactions.description: A silicon hydride adds across a vinyl group — the platinum-catalysed cure of addition silicones (LSR, RTV-2).

tags.role: the silicon — its H migrates to C3; new Si-C2 bond
the vinyl double bond that saturates

reactions.name: Disulfide coupling (peroxide-mediated)
reactions.description: Two thiols couple to a disulfide — the vulcanisation-type S-S bridge — with hydrogen peroxide taking up the two hydrogens as water.

tags.role: the two sulfurs — the new S-S bond
the peroxide oxygens — the O-O bond breaks and each O leaves as a water

reactions.name: Thiol + H2O2 → sulfenic acid + water
reactions.description: The first step of thiol oxidation by hydrogen peroxide: the O–O bond breaks, one OH goes to sulfur, the other leaves as water.

tags.role: the sulfur — gains the OH
the OH that moves to sulfur
the other oxygen — leaves as water

reactions.name: Sulfenic acid + thiol → disulfide + water
reactions.description: The second step of thiol oxidation: a sulfenic acid condenses with a thiol to the disulfide bridge, releasing water.

tags.role: the two sulfurs — the new S–S bond
the OH — leaves as water

reactions.name: Silanol + silanol (siloxane bond)
reactions.description: Two Si-OH groups condense to the Si-O-Si backbone bond plus water — how condensation-cure silicones set.

tags.role: leaves in the water
becomes the Si-O-Si bridge

reactions.name: Silanol + alkoxysilane
reactions.description: A silanol condenses with a methoxysilane, releasing methanol — the moisture-cure (RTV-1) crosslinking step.

tags.role: the silanol oxygen — becomes the bridge
the methoxy oxygen — leaves with its methyl as methanol

reactions.name: Alkoxysilane + water
reactions.description: Moisture hydrolyses Si-OMe to Si-OH — the step that precedes condensation in silane coupling agents and RTV-1.

tags.role: methoxy O — leaves as methanol
water O — becomes the new Si-OH

reactions.name: Phenol + formaldehyde (methylolation)
reactions.description: Formaldehyde substitutes an ortho/para ring hydrogen of phenol, giving a methylol phenol — the first step of every phenolic resin.

tags.role: the reacting ring carbon (para here) — its H moves to the formaldehyde oxygen
the formaldehyde carbon — new bond to the ring

reactions.name: Methylol + phenol (methylene bridge)
reactions.description: A methylol phenol condenses with another phenol ring, expelling water and leaving the CH2 bridge that cures novolacs and resoles.

tags.role: the bridging CH2 carbon
the methylol OH — leaves as water
the ring carbon of the second phenol that is attacked

reactions.name: Urea + formaldehyde
reactions.description: Formaldehyde adds to a urea N-H giving a methylol urea — the start of UF (and, with melamine, MF) resins.

tags.role: the reacting nitrogen
the formaldehyde carbon — new N-C bond; its O becomes OH

reactions.name: Williamson ether (halide + alcohol)
reactions.description: An alkoxide/alcohol displaces a halide to form an ether.

tags.role: the bromine — a leaving atom, expelled as HBr (not drawn)
the attacking oxygen
the carbon where substitution happens

reactions.name: Amine alkylation (halide + amine)
reactions.description: An amine displaces a halide — chain extension and quaternisation chemistry (e.g. ionenes).

tags.role: the bromine — leaves (as HBr, not drawn)
the attacking nitrogen
the substitution carbon

reactions.name: Phenol + epichlorohydrin (glycidylation)
reactions.description: Phenol displaces the chloride of epichlorohydrin, attaching a glycidyl ether — how DGEBA epoxy resin is made from bisphenol-A.

tags.role: the CH2 attacked by the phenol oxygen
the phenol oxygen
the chloride — a leaving atom, expelled as HCl (not drawn)

reactions.note: C1CO1 at the end is the intact epoxide ring, ready for later cure.

reactions.name: Ester hydrolysis
reactions.description: Water splits an ester back into acid + alcohol — polyester degradation.

tags.role: the ester bridge O — leaves with the alkyl as the alcohol
the water O — becomes the acid's new OH

reactions.name: Amide hydrolysis
reactions.description: Water splits an amide into acid + amine — nylon degradation.

tags.role: the amide N — leaves as the free amine
the water O — the acid's new OH

reactions.name: Ester aminolysis
reactions.description: An amine displaces the alkoxy group of an ester, forming an amide — how PET can be chemically recycled to useful amides.

tags.role: the ester O — leaves as the alcohol
the amine N — the new amide bond

reactions.name: Imine / Schiff base (aldehyde + amine)
reactions.description: An aldehyde condenses with a primary amine to an imine (C=N) plus water — dynamic covalent chemistry, vitrimers, self-healing gels.

tags.role: the carbonyl O — leaves in the water
the amine N — replaces it as C=N

reactions.name: Carbonate link (diaryl carbonate + phenol)
reactions.description: A phenol displaces one aryloxide of a diaryl carbonate — the melt transesterification route to polycarbonate.

tags.role: the displaced aryl-ester oxygen — leaves as free phenol
the incoming phenol oxygen — the new carbonate bridge

reactions.name: Epoxide + secondary amine (crosslink step)
reactions.description: The second addition in amine cure: the secondary amine formed by the first addition opens another epoxide, creating the branch point.

tags.role: epoxide O → OH
attacked CH2
the nitrogen — now bonded to three carbons: a crosslink junction

reactions.name: Methylol urea + alcohol (ether cure)
reactions.description: A methylol group condenses with a hydroxyl (e.g. cellulose in wood panels), expelling water — how UF/MF resins bond to the substrate.

tags.role: the bridging CH2
the methylol OH — leaves as water
the substrate oxygen

reactions.name: Carbamate exchange (vitrimer)
reactions.description: A urethane swaps its alkoxy group with a free alcohol — the dynamic bond exchange behind PU vitrimers and reprocessable networks.

tags.role: the old carbamate oxygen — leaves with its ethyl
the incoming alcohol oxygen

reactions.name: Oxime (ketone + hydroxylamine)
reactions.description: A ketone condenses with hydroxylamine to an oxime — the crosslinker chemistry of oxime-cure silicones and PVA gels.

tags.role: the carbonyl O — follow it into the water
the nitrogen — becomes the C=N
